📍 GPS Status?Location & heading come from gpsd. A compass heading is used when the receiver provides one; otherwise heading is inferred from movement (course over ground). With no GPS, all values are 0. Windows has no gpsd of its own: set KRAKEN_GPSD_HOST (and KRAKEN_GPSD_PORT) to one on the network, or use a Static location.

🌐 Web Mapper?Streams DoA bearings to the KrakenSDR web mapper (built in — no separate middleware needed). KrakenPro Cloud relays to map.krakenrf.com and needs your KrakenPro API key; Local Network broadcasts the records to LAN map clients over WebSocket. Each VFO's squelch is respected: with squelch off its bearings always transmit; with squelch on, only while the squelch is open. Callsign & location come from the Station Information panel above.

📝 DoA Recording?Logs the DoA results (bearing, confidence and the lobe of every VFO) to a file on this device's disk (the KrakenPithe receiver's computer), not your browser - for IQ samples or audio use the 📼 IQ & Audio Recorder. Legacy CSV matches DOA_value.html line-for-line; SQLite is a compact, app-readable database for plotting on a map. The interval applies to both formats; below the actual DoA data rate it logs at the data rate, and duplicate frames are never written.

📼 IQ & Audio Recorder?Records to this device's disk (the KrakenPithe receiver's computer):
IQ (coherent mode): the raw samples of every antenna, phase-calibrated - the whole 2.4 MHz (as heimdall sends it, 2 bytes per sample per antenna: 24 MB/s with 5 antennas) or just one VFO's band (much smaller). Saved in the open SigMF format: one recording per antenna + a collection file tying them together, in one folder; downloaded as one .sigmf archive. Open plays a recording back through the receiver - spectrum, VFOs, decoders, DoA, the map - as if the antennas picked it up again.
Audio: what one or more VFOs demodulate (their demod - NBFM / AM / WBFM - or with demod Digital their decoder's voice), a WAV or Opus file per VFO.

A recording stops at its time limit, when you press Stop, or before the drive is full (a reserve is kept free). It doesn't start when it can't fit. An SD card writes ~8-20 MB/s: a full-band recording of 5 antennas is then held in memory and written after it ends - only short ones fit; use the VFO band or a USB SSD for long ones.

📻 Saved Frequencies?Your list of frequencies, kept on the receiver (every browser sees the same list). Click one to tune the selected VFO to it (also its demod, bandwidth and decoder, when the entry has them); the receiver retunes when it is outside the band shown. Each needs a name and a frequency; a category, a location, demod, bandwidth, decoder, tone / code and notes are optional. Group them in categories (⚙ Categories: add your own, rename, recolour). A frequency with a location appears on the 🗺 map: the marker there lists every frequency saved at that place. Saved frequencies are marked on the spectrum (👁 on a category hides its marks); click a mark to tune. ☆ Save on a VFO card saves that VFO's frequency.

Scan: tick the frequencies to scan - or a whole category with the box in its heading (also the frequencies added to it later; untick single ones to leave them out) - and press ▶ Scan. The selected VFO is tuned to each one that is active, received the way the entry says, and heard while it is (plus the Delay). Coherent mode watches one tuner band at a time (the array recalibrates after each retune); independent mode watches a band on every tuner no other VFO is on.

🔐 Digital Decoders?The voice codecs the digital decoders can use, and the installed decoder plugins. Auto detect on a plugin = it runs when a VFO's decoder is on Auto detect (untick the ones you never need: each costs CPU). Plugins are plain source folders (plugins/<id>/): to add one, build it in the KrakenSDR source folder (build_windows.bat - this package has no sources or compiler), copy its kraken_doa_v2\plugins\<id>\build\decoder.exe into the same place in this foldercopy its folder into kraken_doa_v2/plugins/, run make in kraken_doa_v2build_windows.bat (or make in kraken_doa_v2 in the MSYS2 UCRT64 shell) and press ↻. To decode a VFO, tick Digital decoder on it in the Decimators box and pick Auto detect or a decoder; any number of VFOs can decode at once, each with its own tab in the panel under the waterfall. Voice plays with Demod "Digital" (or Listen in the VFO's tab). The AMBE and TETRA codecs are not shipped (licensing): you build them yourself, for personal use - whether that is allowed where you live is your responsibility.

🗂 Decoder Logging?Saves what the digital decoders report (every VFO with a decoder on) to files on this device's disk: one JSON Lines file per day (decoders-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl). At midnight the day's file is closed and gzipped; days older than Keep are deleted (only these files - nothing else in the folder). To spare the SD carddisk the records are collected in memory and written every few seconds; writing pauses when less than 100 MB is free. Raw frames (ADS-B, APRS, POCSAG) can be large - ADS-B near an airport is roughly 100-300 MB a day before gzip.

🗣 Voice to Text?Writes down what is said on the VFOs whose 🗣 Transcribe box is ticked (on the VFO cards above) - any number at once, whichever one you listen to. Analog voice is demodulated with the VFO's demod (NBFM / AM / WBFM); a VFO with its digital decoder on gives the decoded voice (P25, DMR, D-STAR, NXDN, TETRA - the voice codec must be installed). It runs on this device with a free speech-to-text model (OpenAI's Whisper, via whisper.cpp): nothing is sent anywhere. Each transmission is cut out by the VFO's squelch (with the squelch off: while a signal stands 10 dB over the noise), or by the decoder's voice frames and talker changes, and is transcribed when it ends - a few seconds later. Noise and data bursts are skipped (voice activity detection). The transcripts are in the 🗣 Voice tab under the waterfall - with the talker's ID for digital radios, the bearing in coherent mode with DoA on, and the audio to check them - and go to the Decoder Logging files when that is on (type "Voice transcripts").

🧪 Experimental?Features that are still being developed and tested: they may change, and may not work well at every site yet.

▶
✈ Array Calibration?Uses ADS-B aircraft as transmitters at known positions to measure what the noise-source calibration can't see: cable length differences between the antennas, where each antenna really stands, and how the whole array is turned (mounting / heading).

Needs: a VFO with the ADS-B decoder (1090 MHz) and DoA on, the station location and heading (Station Information: a static location, or GPS with a compass), the array standing still. Press Collect and leave it running while aircraft come from many directions (tens of minutes at a busy site, longer elsewhere).

The result is checked on aircraft it wasn't fitted on. Apply uses it for MUSIC and beamforming on every frequency: delays and positions carry over. Differences between the antennas themselves (and multipath) don't - they show as "Unexpl.". The calibration belongs to this array setup: change the radius or elements and it is not used.
No calibration in use.

🧪 Debug Playback?Plays a decoder's synthetic test transmission (several transmitters with known IDs at known bearings on a 5-element UCA) through the real receiver as if the antennas had picked it up: spectrum, waterfall, VFO, decoder, DoA and the map's 📡 DF panel - to see and check a decoder without the real signal.

While it plays: heimdall's data is disconnected and nothing is sent to heimdall; the frequency / gain can't be changed; your settings are not saved - the VFO, decoder and array set up for the playback are a sandbox, and Stop puts your own settings back (also after a restart). Nothing goes out either: web mapper, decoder log, Voice to Text, DoA recording, incidents are paused.

Generate builds a test transmission once (the plugins' own generators, a few seconds of CPU; kept in testsignal_cache/). Check compares the bearings in the DF panel with the ones the test transmission was made with.
